text.text_excerpt: Like all of the food tours in various cities we've taken, this one was again one of the top highlights of our vacation. It's a great way to get to know the city, experience local cuisine, and hear some history of the restaurants and the city. Earlier in the day, we had taken a carriage ride/tour and it was horrendous. No history whatsoever. Our guide merely read restaurant/shop signs as he passed by them. My favorite? "Huge Ass Beer." Yeah, thanks, buddy. I can read. Therefore, experiencing the French Quarter Culinary History and Tasting Tour was like night and day. Our guide was fantastic. She was very friendly, informative, and gave a COMPLETE history of the locations we visited and the...

We had a wonderful time on this tour. Renee was our guide and she was so knowledgeable about food and New Orleans in general. We were very grateful for her input and took her advice on some additional places to eat during our stay. Her recommendations were spot on. The tour goes through a number of restaurants - including historic restaurants like Antoine's and Brennan's. The sample portions are generous and give a good sampling of traditional fare. We tried gumbo, shrimp remoulade, pralines, red beans and rice, etc. The tour also goes to Leah's for pralines and we were given a coupon for a free praline with the purchase of twelve. I can't recommend this tour enough! If you are new to NOLA, and you are interested in learning about the vast fascinating culinary tradition, along with the amazing history of the places and people who shaped it, this tour is what you're looking for. Our guide, Renee, was lovely - funny, articulate, and a true lover of NOLA culture and history. She loved to tell stories, and she was very attentive to everyone's questions and interests. Quick note: you shouldn't be starving before the tour. I'd eat a small brunch beforehand. We got a small portion of every food.
